$comment: Conformance traceability manifest (#245). Each requirement row maps one normative clause (or one facet of a multi-part clause) to its observable conformance assertion and the tests that drive it. Validated by scripts/check-conformance-manifest.mjs: unknown anchors, quoted clauses missing from their anchored section, duplicate IDs, missing tests, and coverage states inconsistent with their mappings all fail CI; rows not fully tested are the visible outstanding report, never silent. observation.local records this implementation's chosen behavior where the spec permits more than one; a local pin never becomes the protocol requirement. Rows whose applicability names a capability apply only where the deployment claims it: a runner MUST NOT mark an unclaimed capability nonconforming, and a failed SHOULD row is a recorded departure, not a hard fail. source.revision names the drafts revision the rows were evaluated against; the stale-text check catches edits, the revision identifies the edition.

requirements.text: The AS MUST reject with `invalid_request` a `mission_intent` presented on a front-channel authorization request that does not use a PAR-issued `request_uri`

observation.normative: authorization request carrying mission_intent without a PAR-issued request_uri fails invalid_request

requirements.text: a `mission_intent` submitted outside the Request Object in the same push MUST be rejected with `invalid_request`

observation.normative: push carrying a Request Object plus a mission_intent outside it fails invalid_request

requirements.text: The AS MUST bound the Submission envelope's total size, the Intent's total size and the lengths of its arrays, and the count and per-entry sizes of `evidence` entries, refusing a submission that exceeds the deployment-defined limits with `invalid_request`

observation.normative: submission exceeding the declared evidence entry count or per-entry size fails invalid_request
observation.local: driven at the intake parser, not through the PAR endpoint

tests.name: Intent Submission Evidence intake, stage 1 (@spec mission#intent-submission-evidence) > bounds the entry COUNT (config default, overridable)
Intent Submission Evidence intake, stage 1 (@spec mission#intent-submission-evidence) > bounds the per-entry SIZE (config default, overridable)

requirements.text: The AS MUST bound the Submission envelope's total size, the Intent's total size and the lengths of its arrays, and the count and per-entry sizes of `evidence` entries, refusing a submission that exceeds the deployment-defined limits with `invalid_request`

observation.normative: submission exceeding the declared envelope total size, Intent total size, or Intent array-length bounds fails invalid_request at the wire

requirements.text: the AS MUST ignore any `mission_intent`, `authorization_details`, `scope`, or `resource` presented, and MUST NOT let such a value widen the authority derived from the pushed parameters

observation.normative: widened mission_intent, authorization_details, scope, or resource beside the request_uri on the authorization request neither affects approval rendering nor widens issued authority

requirements.text: an object carrying duplicate member names is rejected at parse time, before the parsed data model exists

observation.normative: input destined for commitment carrying duplicate JSON member names is rejected before canonicalization; last-value-wins is foreclosed

tests.name: intent validation (@spec mission#submission-via-par) > rejects duplicate member names
Submission envelope parse (@spec mission#submission-via-par) > strict parse: duplicate member names in the envelope are refused
parseStrictJson > rejects duplicate member names (core § canonicalization)

requirements.text: A verifier MUST reject a digest whose algorithm prefix it does not recognize

observation.normative: an anchor with an unrecognized algorithm prefix is rejected, never treated as sha-256

tests.name: integrity anchors (core § test-vectors) > verifyAnchor round-trips and rejects unknown algorithm prefixes

requirements.text: An AS MUST reject `max_derivations` below 1 with `invalid_request`

observation.normative: controls.max_derivations of 0 or less fails invalid_request
observation.local: the kernel test drives the input but asserts a message regex; the invalid_request code is not yet asserted

tests.name: intent validation (@spec mission#submission-via-par) > rejects max_derivations below 1

requirements.text: the AS MUST maintain a per-Mission count of **derivations** and MUST refuse with `invalid_grant` any derivation that would exceed the bound

observation.normative: derivation past controls.max_derivations fails invalid_grant at the token endpoint
observation.local: covered at the kernel gate only; no wire test observes invalid_grant for exhaustion

tests.name: lifecycle (@spec status#legal-transitions) > gates derivation on state and derivation cap (@spec mission#lifecycle)

requirements.text: A derivation that fails, including one refused for exceeding the bound, MUST NOT be counted

observation.normative: a failed or refused derivation leaves the derivation count unchanged
observation.local: asserted on the expansion nothing_to_expand refusal path; not yet driven at the cap boundary itself

tests.name: expansion wire: NON-WIDENING request is REFUSED (@spec expansion#nothing-to-expand) > a pure subset request refuses (invalid_request + nothing_to_expand): predecessor stays active, nothing created or reserved, no derivation consumed

requirements.text: the AS SHOULD include, alongside `error`, the `mission_error` token-error-response member

observation.normative: lifecycle refusals carry mission_error with one of mission_revoked, mission_expired, mission_superseded, derivations_exhausted
observation.local: implementation emits mission_denial_reason with the kernel reason set instead; recorded SHOULD-level departure, tracked in #526

requirements.text: an AS whose policy cannot accept the proposed `expires_at` refuses with `invalid_authorization_details` rather than rewriting it

observation.normative: unacceptable proposed expires_at fails invalid_authorization_details; the AS never rewrites the value

requirements.notes: Cross-document contradiction with the Mission Template three-way clamp; no test pins either behavior until #525 resolves.

requirements.text: The mapping is a lookup, never synthesis; the AS refuses an Intent that matches no configured mapping with `invalid_authorization_details`

observation.normative: in configured-mapping (template) mode, an Intent matching no configured mapping fails invalid_authorization_details, distinguishable from a policy refusal

requirements.notes: Core configured-mapping mode, not the Mission Template companion; the companion's unknown template_id error is specified and tested separately.

requirements.text: an AS MUST NOT derive Mission-bound authority from a client-supplied `mission_id`

observation.normative: a client-supplied mission_id cannot select or alter the Mission used for derivation; if the request is accepted, the emitted Mission is the grant-bound Mission (rejecting the unexpected parameter also conforms)

requirements.text: A credential the Mission Issuer derives MUST have an `exp` that does not exceed the Mission's `expires_at`

observation.normative: no derived credential's exp exceeds the Mission's expires_at
observation.local: driven on the async-delegation initial-access path; the requirement spans every credential the issuer derives (refresh, exchange, deferral, child, expansion), so the remaining paths are outstanding

tests.name: async-delegation terminal paths (@spec async-delegation) > absolute-lifetime clamp: the initial access token exp never exceeds the Mission expires_at

requirements.text: The AS MUST NOT issue a Mission-bound token whose `scope` exceeds the Authority Set

observation.normative: every issued scope value corresponds to authority present in authorization_details; no issued token carries scope beyond the Authority Set

requirements.text: the AS MUST return `active: false` and include `mission.state` giving the reason

observation.normative: a valid token on a revoked or expired Mission introspects as active: false plus mission.state
observation.local: provider currently returns bare {active:false} with no mission member; red-first tests and the paired fix are #526

requirements.text: MUST authenticate the calling party

observation.normative: an unauthenticated introspection caller receives no Mission detail

requirements.text: MUST return Mission data only to a caller authorized to receive it, in particular a Resource Server that is an audience of the token

observation.normative: a caller not authorized for the token receives no Mission detail

requirements.text: MUST audience-filter the response, returning the `authorization_details` entries and Mission data relevant to the caller's audience and not disclosing entries addressed to other audiences

observation.normative: the response discloses only the entries and Mission data relevant to the caller's audience
observation.local: no audience filtering exists in the handler; red-first tests and the paired fix are #526

requirements.text: the **Authority Set entry commitment**, the envelope above with `typ` `mission-authority-entry`, `iss` the Mission `issuer`, and `value` a single Authority Set entry object exactly as recorded

observation.normative: the displayed entry reproduces the displayed digest exactly, and member insertion order does not change the digest

tests.name: Authority Set entry commitment (@spec mission#integrity-anchors) > reproduces the core test vector exactly
Authority Set entry commitment (@spec mission#integrity-anchors) > resolves different member insertion order to the same digest

requirements.text: Authorization for `discharge` requires a distinct `mission_discharge` scope or an equivalent deployment-defined grant.

observation.normative: a discharge request from a caller with no distinct mission_discharge grant (or deployment-defined equivalent) is refused, never treated as authorized

requirements.notes: Planned test surface: authorization-server integration test for the discharge operation, asserting refusal for a caller holding mission_lifecycle but not mission_discharge.

requirements.text: or being the Mission's Subject, Approver, or an administrator, MUST NOT by itself imply discharge authority

observation.normative: a caller who is the Mission's Subject, Approver, or an administrator, but lacks the distinct discharge grant, is refused a discharge request

requirements.notes: Planned test surface: authorization-server integration test for the discharge operation, asserting refusal for the Subject/Approver/administrator role alone.

requirements.text: An unknown `mission_id`, an unknown `entry_digest`, an unknown `condition_digest`, an entry with no `terminal_when`, an `event_type` that does not match the condition `condition_digest` names, and a caller not authorized for that target all collapse to the endpoint's existing `not_found` treatment

observation.normative: an unknown mission_id, entry_digest, or condition_digest, an entry carrying no terminal_when, an event_type that does not match the condition condition_digest names, and an unauthorized-target caller all produce the identical not_found response

requirements.notes: Planned test surface: authorization-server integration test asserting identical not_found bodies across the six anti-oracle cases.

requirements.text: a mismatch joins the `not_found` collapse, since distinguishing it would reveal information about a condition selected by digest

observation.normative: an event_type that does not match the condition named by condition_digest joins the not_found collapse rather than receiving a distinguishing error

requirements.notes: Planned test surface: authorization-server integration test for the discharge operation, mismatched event_type/condition_digest pair, asserting a not_found response indistinguishable from the other collapse cases.

requirements.text: One `entry_digest` discharges every recorded entry resolving to that digest as a single equivalence-class transition, and therefore one version increment

observation.normative: discharging one of several byte-identical Mission-record entries discharges all of them as one equivalence-class transition with exactly one version increment

requirements.notes: Planned test surface: authorization-server integration test with two byte-identical entries, asserting a single discharge and a single version increment.

requirements.text: retransmit carrying a `nonce` already seen for that client and `mission_id`, together with a request byte-identical to the original, the AS MUST replay the original response rather than re-execute the operation.

observation.normative: a retransmitted lifecycle request with the same nonce and byte-identical body replays the original signed response rather than re-executing the operation

requirements.notes: Planned test surface: authorization-server lifecycle-endpoint idempotency test, same-nonce same-body retransmit.

requirements.text: The same `nonce` paired with a request that is not byte-identical to the original MUST be refused `invalid_request`

observation.normative: a retransmitted nonce paired with a non-identical request body is refused invalid_request, never answered with the unrelated original response

requirements.notes: Planned test surface: authorization-server lifecycle-endpoint idempotency test, same-nonce different-body retransmit.

requirements.text: The stored signed response is returned verbatim, per the `nonce` rule above.

observation.normative: a discharge retransmission with the same nonce and a byte-identical request returns the stored signed response verbatim, unchanged, including its original nonce

requirements.notes: Planned test surface: authorization-server discharge idempotency test, same nonce and byte-identical request, asserting the identical prior signed envelope is returned.

requirements.text: It issues a new signed envelope that echoes the new `nonce` and carries the stored operation result: the same `outcome` and selectors, and the original `prior_version` and `current_version` the first commit produced.

observation.normative: a repeated discharge request sharing (discharge authority, mission_id, entry_digest, condition_digest, event_id) and the same assertion fingerprint but a new nonce performs no state-changing work and returns a freshly signed envelope echoing the new nonce, carrying the stored outcome, selectors, and the original prior_version and current_version

requirements.notes: Planned test surface: authorization-server discharge idempotency test, same event tuple and fingerprint, different nonce, asserting a fresh envelope (not the original signed response) carrying the original versions and no re-latch.

requirements.text: the same tuple with a different fingerprint is refused `conflict`

observation.normative: the same (discharge authority, mission_id, entry_digest, condition_digest, event_id) tuple asserted with a different event assertion fingerprint is refused conflict

requirements.notes: Planned test surface: authorization-server discharge idempotency test, same event tuple, changed evidence_ref/observed_at.

requirements.text: the same `event_id` asserted against another Mission, entry, or condition is a valid, independent assertion, since one real-world event legitimately fans out to more than one target.

observation.normative: reusing the same event_id against a different mission_id, entry_digest, or condition_digest is processed as an independent discharge, not refused as a duplicate or conflict

requirements.notes: Planned test surface: authorization-server discharge idempotency test, same event_id across two distinct Missions.

requirements.text: MUST NOT discharge the entry again or increment the version again

observation.normative: a delivery presenting any valid condition against an already-discharged entry, whether a sibling condition or the same condition under a different event_id, is acknowledged already_discharged without re-latching the entry or incrementing the state version

requirements.notes: Planned test surface: authorization-server discharge test, both a sibling condition and the same condition under a different event_id, against an already-discharged entry.

requirements.text: A delivery reaching the endpoint after `completed`, `revoked`, `expired`, or another terminal state returns an authenticated `terminal_noop` acknowledgement

observation.normative: a discharge request against a Mission already in a terminal state returns terminal_noop with no transition and no version increment

requirements.notes: Planned test surface: authorization-server discharge test against a revoked/expired/completed Mission.

requirements.text: `discharge` applies while the Mission is `active` or `suspended`: a suspended Mission still narrows monotonically.

observation.normative: a discharge request against a suspended Mission succeeds and narrows the entry exactly as it would for an active Mission

requirements.notes: Planned test surface: authorization-server discharge test against a suspended Mission.

requirements.text: one of `discharged` (this request committed the latch), `already_discharged` (a sibling condition, or the same condition under a different `event_id`, presented against an already-latched entry), or `terminal_noop` (the Mission was already in a terminal state).

observation.normative: the signed discharge_result's outcome member is discharged, already_discharged, or terminal_noop matching the actual transition, alongside entry_digest, condition_digest, event_id, prior_version, and current_version

requirements.notes: Planned test surface: authorization-server discharge test, asserting the discharge_result shape and outcome value for each of the three outcomes.

requirements.text: The entry latch (or its equivalence-class latch), the version increment, the audit and result record, and the durable propagation work (an outbox entry or a signal enqueue) commit as one unit.

observation.normative: the entry latch, version increment, audit and result record, and durable propagation work (outbox entry or signal enqueue) are never observed partially committed under concurrent or interrupted delivery

requirements.notes: Planned test surface: authorization-server concurrency test, concurrent duplicate discharge requests racing the same entry.

requirements.text: the child-delegation profile's entry-wise propagation to an already-justified Child Mission

observation.normative: a Child Mission's derivation consults, or is otherwise gated by, the committed parent latch until child materialization completes, so a Child Mission already justified by a parent entry cannot derive that entry once the parent's discharge commit lands, even though the child-delegation profile's own materialization is asynchronous
observation.local: requires the deployment to also adopt the child-delegation profile

requirements.notes: Planned test surface: cross-component test spanning the discharge operation and child-delegation derivation gating, racing a child derivation against the parent's discharge commit before materialization completes.

requirements.text: The AS MUST resolve and validate the selector whenever a condition first enters an immutable Mission-record entry

observation.normative: discharge_policy is resolved and validated whenever a condition enters an immutable Mission-record entry, including a condition a derived entry adds after activation (child creation, expansion, or another derivation), refusing the Intent or derivation when the selector maps to nothing

requirements.notes: Planned test surface: authorization-server integration test asserting discharge_policy resolution/refusal for a condition introduced by a derivation after Mission activation (child creation or expansion), not only at initial approval.

requirements.text: The AS MUST NOT dereference `evidence_ref` in baseline processing and MUST NOT treat either member as authorization input.

observation.normative: the AS never dereferences evidence_ref during baseline discharge processing and never treats evidence_ref or evidence_digest as input to an authorization decision

requirements.notes: Planned test surface: authorization-server discharge test asserting no outbound fetch of evidence_ref and no authorization-decision dependency on either evidence member.

requirements.text: The AS validates selector existence (`mission_id`, `entry_digest`, and `condition_digest` all resolve, the entry carries `terminal_when`, and `event_type` matches the named condition), then condition membership (the named condition belongs to the named entry), then target authorization

observation.normative: the AS checks selector existence, condition membership, and target authorization before returning terminal_noop, so a terminal Mission cannot be used to test whether a selector resolves

requirements.notes: Planned test surface: authorization-server discharge test against a terminal Mission with an unknown entry_digest or condition_digest, asserting the not_found collapse rather than terminal_noop.

requirements.text: before further consequential reliance when an in-order event carries `authority_changed` true, even when `state` equals `prior_state` and no version gap exists.

observation.normative: a consumer that receives an in-order mission.lifecycle-change event with authority_changed true rematerializes its effective authority view via Mission Status before further consequential reliance, even with state unchanged and no version gap

requirements.notes: Planned test surface: signals consumer-behavior test, in-order active-to-active event carrying authority_changed true.

requirements.text: a Mission Issuer MUST emit `authority_changed` true on the `mission.lifecycle-change` event a discharge commit produces

observation.normative: a Mission Issuer that commits a discharge and emits Signals events sets authority_changed true on the mission.lifecycle-change event the commit produces
observation.local: requires the deployment to also adopt the Status profile's completion/discharge capability

requirements.notes: Planned test surface: cross-component test spanning the discharge operation and Signals event emission, asserting authority_changed true on the produced event.

requirements.text: a Mission Issuer MUST NOT deliver a `mission.lifecycle-change` event whose effective-authority change is represented by `authority_changed` alone (a discharge commit, {{I-D.draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-status}}) to a stream whose consumer has not declared `authority_changed` in `mission_capabilities_supported`

observation.normative: a stream whose consumer has not declared authority_changed in mission_capabilities_supported never receives a mission.lifecycle-change event carrying authority_changed true
observation.local: requires the deployment to also adopt the Status profile's completion/discharge capability

requirements.notes: Planned test surface: signals delivery test, discharge commit against a stream lacking the authority_changed capability declaration, asserting no event delivered on that stream.
